title: AI Cryptanalysis Agents Cut 1024-Bit RSA Oracle Forgery 3.5× & Introduce Fan Factories
aiSystem: Google DeepMind Cryptanalysis Agent Harness + Lean 4
whyItMatters: DeepMind AI agents wrote 33,500 lines of code in under 4 days to cut a 5-month 1024-bit RSA signature forgery cost by 3.5× and proved Lean-checked Fan Factories cutting batch factoring cost ~30× per key.
summary: On November 6, 2026, Google DeepMind (Dj Dvijotham, Abhradeep Thakurta, Pushmeet Kohli) with cryptographers Nadia Heninger (UCSD/Inria) and Emmanuel Thomé (Inria) released two cryptanalysis working papers—Modular Roots from a Restricted Oracle and Fan Factories. In a sandboxed 1024-bit RSA benchmark, two supervised AI agents wrote 33,500 lines of C++, CUDA, and Python across 336 distributed experiments (16,292 tool calls) in 3 days 22 hours with ~20 human approval messages, cutting CPU cost 3.5× (391 vs. 1,380 core-years) while proposing a theoretical ~1,600× improvement for 32-byte digests. Separately, a two-agent prover/verifier harness formalized Fan Factories in Lean 4, improving Coppersmith’s 1993 batch-factoring exponent from L[1.9019] to L[1.7929] (~30× cheaper per extra 1024-bit key after precomputation).
technicalHighlights: Two supervised AI agents autonomously wrote 33,500 lines of C++/CUDA/Python, ran 336 distributed jobs (up to 300,000 CPU cores & 16 GPUs), diagnosed a 32-bit overflow bug, and reduced 1024-bit RSA oracle forgery from 1,380 to 391 CPU core-years in 3 days 22 hours.
Derived a theoretical ~1,600× improvement for forging 1024-bit RSA signatures when an attacker controls only a 32-byte digest under a restricted signing oracle.

Introduced Lean 4-checked Fan Factories (multiple number fields sharing one rational precomputation), lowering the batch-NFS exponent from L[1.9019] to L[1.7929] (~1/58 of single-key GNFS cost per extra 1024-bit target).
caveats: Both papers are unrefereed working papers targeting deprecated 1024-bit RSA keys; 2048-bit and larger RSA deployments remain secure. The 1,600× and 30× figures are leading-order theoretical estimates, no Fan Factory has been implemented, and the 3.5× speedup is an implementation/sieving optimization rather than a new factoring algorithm.

scoreRationale.foundational: Improves Coppersmith’s 1993 multiple-target factorization factory exponent with Lean-checked algebra and advances affine-oracle RSA cryptanalysis.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrates that autonomous AI agents can compress months of elite distributed cryptanalysis engineering into under four days, accelerating legacy RSA-1024 retirement.
scoreRationale.verification: The 391 core-year 1024-bit forged root was empirically verified and Fan Factories algebra was machine-checked in Lean 4, though both working papers await external peer review.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed a 5-month academic cryptanalysis campaign into 3 days 22 hours with ~20 human approval messages.
